title: xDrip sometimes is not able to reconnect to tomato after not being connected for some time.
body:
Happening with lineageos 14.1 on nexus5 (20180405)
Finally got a repro of this with the BT sniffer showing what is happening:

High level description:
After not being connected for some time (half an hour to my thinking, but more than a day according to the logs). I brought the phone close to the tomato. It did not connect for ~15 minutes.
I opened the phone, and in a few seconds they connected.

The connection has happened on 17/4 on ~9:05.

Looking at the sniffer logs, then the phone sends BT SCAN_REQ, the tomato answers with SCAN_RSP
[by the way, sometimes the tomato does not answer.]

31034	2018-04-17 21:05:15.186786	47:49:54:8e:fd:2b	db:23:f4:f2:86:62	LE LL	38	SCAN_REQ
31035	2018-04-17 21:05:15.192240	db:23:f4:f2:86:62	Broadcast	LE LL	32	SCAN_RSP

The phone does not send a connection request.

After the phone is opened, it sends a connection request. and all is well.
It takes ~10 seconds from the connect request to the last scan request, so I'm not sure if the scan is part of the connect or not.

Looking at the xdrip logs, here is what I see:

"2018-04-17 21:03:32"	"DexCollectionService"	"onState change status = 133"
"2018-04-17 21:03:32"	"DexCollectionService"	"onConnectionStateChange: State disconnected."
"2018-04-17 21:03:32"	"DexCollectionService"	"onConnectionStateChange: mBluetoothGatt is not null, closing."
"2018-04-17 21:03:32"	"DexCollectionService"	"Refresh result state close: true"
"2018-04-17 21:03:32"	"DexCollectionService"	"onConnectionStateChange: Disconnected from GATT server."
"2018-04-17 21:03:32"	"DexCollectionService"	"Scheduling next retry in: 36 seconds @ 2018-04-17 21:04:08 period diff: -1523988007150"
"2018-04-17 21:03:32"	"DexCollectionService"	"setRetryTimer: Restarting in: 36 seconds"

But when phone is opened, here are the logs:
"2018-04-17 21:05:23"	"DexCollectionService"	"setFailoverTimer: Fallover Restarting in: 6 minutes"
"2018-04-17 21:05:23"	"DexCollectionService"	"checkConnection: Connection state: DISCONNECTED"
"2018-04-17 21:05:23"	"DexCollectionService"	"connect: going to connect to device at address: DB:23:F4:F2:86:62"
"2018-04-17 21:05:23"	"DexCollectionService"	"connect: Trying to create a new connection."
"2018-04-17 21:05:23"	"DexCollectionService"	"Scheduling next retry in: 39 seconds @ 2018-04-17 21:06:02 period diff: -1523988118254"
"2018-04-17 21:05:23"	"DexCollectionService"	"setRetryTimer: Restarting in: 39 seconds"
"2018-04-17 21:05:24"	"DexCollectionService"	"onState change status = 0"
"2018-04-17 21:05:24"	"DexCollectionService"	"onConnectionStateChange: Connected to GATT server. "
"2018-04-17 21:05:24"	"DexCollectionService"	"Requesting to discover services: previous: NULL"
"2018-04-17 21:05:24"	"DexCollectionService"	"checkConnection: Connection state: CONNECTED"

comments.body:
Attached is the bt capture (in a zip file), and the xdrip log.
For the first time only you open Wireshark:
    go to edit->preferences->protocols->DLT_USER
    edit the encapsulation table and add "user10 (DLT=147)" with "nordic_ble" in payload protocol field.

After some more reading, and searching in the internet it is hard to be very optimistic.
There are many implementations of android BT.

Following https://devzone.nordicsemi.com/cfs-file/__key/communityserver-blogs-components-weblogfiles/00-00-00-00-04-DZ-1046/2604.BLE_5F00_on_5F00_Android_5F00_v1.0.1.pdf it seems that many things make a difference here:

1) autoconnect parameter of phone.
2) bonded or not.
3) device was already scanned or not.

I was not bonded and in my code autoconnect was false. It has now changed to true. so I'll keep following.

I see this one quite frequently with miaomiao (including on my old (Mate 10 Pro) and new (Oneplus 6t) phones).  XDrip reports the status as `133 (restart device?)`.  When this happens, rescanning/reselecting the miaomiao from the "bluetooth" menu option, and restarting the collector always seems to work.

Just a hunch based entirely on generic software/hardware knowledge rather than miaomiao/tomato specifics, but I guess the 133 code might mean "rebooting; wait and reconnect" (or just "connection invalid; re-do bluetooth handshake") or something like that?

Doing so seems to work, either way.  Perhaps XDrip could try handling status 133 that way, at least by default, until we know more?  Don't see it doing any harm since there's no data coming in anyway.

@tzachi-dar What is the status of this issue?  Would you please update?
Thanks
